summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(f) read with Sections 79(1)(c) & (d), 38, 39, 40, and 60 of the Electricity Act, 2003 concerning the unjust, arbitrary and illegal terms imposed by Himachal Pradesh Power Transmission Corporation Limited and Allain Duhangan Hydro Power Limited for transmission of power by the Petitioner on inter-state transmission lines operated by them. The Petitioner, Kanchanjunga Power Company Private Limited (“hereinafter referred to as “KPCPL”), has filed the present Petition with the following prayers: “a. _Declare that the terms of the Interim Power Transmission Agreements dated 28.04.2016 between the Petitioner and the Respondents No.1 and 2 as well as the invoices issued thereunder are void and non-est insofar as they are inconsistent with the applicable inter-state transmission regulations including the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Open Access in inter-State Transmission) Regulations, 2008, Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2010 and Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2014;_ _e. Direct the Respondents to refund to the Petitioner all amounts collected for the use of the 220 kV Fozal pooling station, the 220 kV D/C line from the Fozal pooling station to the LILO point on the 220 kV Pirni-Nallagarh D/C transmission line and the 220 kV Pirni-Nallagarh D/C transmission line in excess of the transmission tariff determined by this Hon’ble Commission;_ _f. Pending the instant Petition, restrain the Respondents from taking any coercive steps, or from interfering with the Petitioner’s use of the 220 kV Fozal pooling station, the 220 kV D/C line from the Fozal pooling station to the LILO point on the 220 kV Pirni-Nallagarh D/C transmission line and the 220 kV Pirni-Nallagarh D/C transmission line;_ _h. Pass such other orders that this Commission deems fit in the interest of justice.”_ 2. The instant Petition was first listed for the hearing on 20.6.2017. During the course of the hearing, the Commission observed that the present Petition pertains to the use of the 220 kV Fozal pooling station and the 220 kV D/C line from the Fozal pooling station to the Loop-in-Loop-out (LILO) point on the 220 kV Pirni-Nallagarh D/C transmission line operated by Allain Duhangan Hydro Power Limited, and the charges being levied thereunder by HPPTCL and ADHPL. Accordingly, vide Record of Proceedings dated 20.6.2017, the Petitioner was directed to pay 80% of the outstanding invoices raised by ADHPL/HPPTCL and continue paying monthly charges, subject to adjustment upon final determination of the tariff. Further, the parties were directed to file their replies and rejoinders. 3. The matter was argued at length by the learned senior counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondents. During the course of the hearing, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner referred to the findings of the Commission in its order dated 17.10.2019 in Petition No. 209/MP/2017 filed by AD Hydro, wherein the Commission, _inter alia_ , had held that the AD line is incidental to the inter-State Transmission System and accordingly, determined the transmission charges for the said line. The matter was thereafter reserved for orders on the same day. 5. Aggrieved by the order dated 17.10.2019 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 209/MP/2017, the Petitioner approached the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (hereinafter referred to as “the APTEL”) on the ground that transmission tariff determined by the Commission for the 220 kV Transmission Line built by M/s AD Hydro Power Limited was in violation of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2010, the Act, and the observations of both the APTEL and the Hon'ble Supreme Court. The Petitioner specifically argued that, despite the transmission line being part of the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS), the recovery of transmission charges should be conducted in accordance with the Point of Connection (hereinafter referred to as “PoC”) mechanism. 7. Subsequently, the Commission, vide order dated 19.1.2024 in Petition No. 209/MP/2017, directed inclusion of the AD Line under the Sharing mechanism in accordance with the Sharing Regulations. The relevant extract of the order dated - _(a) The Petitioner shall furnish the transmission charges and losses received by it from AD Hydro, EPPL and KPPTCL (on behalf of KPCPL,_ _(f) After the issue of the tariff order in respect of the subject transmission line pursuant to the order of the APTEL dated 31.8.2023 in Appeal No.410 of 2019, the transmission charges of the subject transmission line shall be recovered in accordance with Regulation 15(2)(a) of Sharing Regulations, 2020._ _(g) Transmission Losses shall be recovered/adjusted in accordance with para 63 of this order._ ” 8. In addition, the Petitioner, being aggrieved by the order dated 26.6.2020 passed 9. Aggrieved by the said decision of the APTEL, the Petitioner filed Civil Appeal No. 5146 of 2024 in the Hon`ble Supreme Court. Vide order dated 3.5.2024, the Hon’ble Supreme Court dismissed the said Civil Appeal. The relevant extract of the said Judgment is as under: 10. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 30.4.2025, has submitted that in view of the above developments, the issues arising in the present Petition stand resolved and the Petition has been rendered infructuous. The Petitioner has prayed to dispose of the instant Petition accordingly. 11. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. According to the Petitioner, pursuant to the judgments of the APTEL and the Hon`ble Supreme Court, the issues arising in the instant Petition stand resolved. Accordingly, the instant Petition is disposed of as infructuous.
